chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isa from Abbas the servant of al-Rida from Abu'l Hasan al-Rida from his father (peace be upon them both). He said:

Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) would say: Whoever says, when he hears the call to the morning prayer: "O Allah, I ask You by the commencement of Your day, the passing of Your night, the attendance of those at Your prayer, and the voices of those who supplicate to You, to forgive me. Surely, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful" — and whoever says the like of that when he hears the call to the Maghrib prayer, then dies on that day or on that night, he will be a forgiven one.

key_terms.أذان الصبح: the call to the morning prayer (Fajr adhan)
key_terms.أذان المغرب: the call to the Maghrib prayer (sunset adhan)
key_terms.التواب الرحيم: the Forgiving, the Merciful — two divine names emphasizing Allah's acceptance of repentance

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when hearing the call to prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the 8th and 7th Imams back to Imam al-Sadiq, teaches a powerful supplication to be recited upon hearing the adhan for the morning (Fajr) and evening (Maghrib) prayers. The supplication asks Allah for forgiveness by invoking the sacred transitions of day and night, the presence of worshippers, and the voices of those calling to prayer. The promise attached is remarkable: whoever dies on the day or night after reciting this prayer will die in a state of repentance.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Muhamad b. `Isa from `Abbas the servant of al-Rida from Abi’l Hasna al-Rida from his father (as). He said:

Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) would say: Whoever says, when he hears the call to the morning prayer: “O Allah! I ask You by the commencement of Your day, the maintenance of Your night, the attendance of those praying to You, and the voices of those supplicating to You, to forgive me. Surely, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful (allahumma inni as’aluka bi iqbali naharik, wa idbari laylatik, wa huduri salatik, wa aswati du`a’ik an tatub `alay, innaka anta ‘tawab al-rahim)” – whoever says that [when he hears the call to the morning prayer or] when he hears the call to Maghrib prayer and dies on that day or on that night, he will be forgiven.
